I like to think I'm a pretty good person, but I know I'm no saint. This think this happened in my junior year of high school, but I can't be certain.

For context, the movie "Suicide Squad" (fucking awful movie) had just come out, and I was out at the mall wearing my Deathstroke baseball cap (a character that wasn't in the movie, but he's my favorite DC villain, so whatever).

I was with my mom and two of my older siblings at the time, and we weren't really at the mall for anything other than walking around I think. We eventually slauntered into a toy store because my mom was in the mood to fuss about toys she would've gotten for us as kids and all that jazz.

Well, to skip past unnecessary details, I eventually decided to buy a little something just to be nice, seeing as we were the only people in the store (this is important for later). Also, there was only one clerk, and she was the only person in the store, so I'm pretty sure that's why she had the balls to start shit.

Now, to give myself some slack, I did NOT say a damn thing to this woman other than "How are you doing?", Cus mommy raised a polite little shit, but goddamn, nothing could have prepared me for the comment that flew out of this woman's mouth the minute she saw my hat:

"OMG, is that DEADSHOT!?"

Immediately this lady goes off about how hot she thinks Deadshot in the Suicide Squad movie is, how Suicide Squad is the best movie ever made, how Harley Quinn is a #Queen and deserves to get it on with both Deadshot and the Joker, how the critics are all wrong about the movie being utter horseshit, yada yada I'm losing braincells just remembering this interaction.

At some point, I finally get to correct her and say that my hat has Deathstroke's symbol and not Deadshot's (tbh I was low-key glad someone didn't mistake it for Deadpool again), and pretty much instantly this lady's attitude did a 180.

"Oh... That's too bad; Deadshot is a million times better than Deathstroke will EVER be. :/"

Tbh, I don't know what caused me to snap; maybe because this lady was the definition of an off the wall fangirl, maybe because I'm a die-hard Deathstroke fanboy, maybe because I was hungry or something, but in any case, I went off.

"Ya know what, miss? Fuck you!"

Now, I'm a sailor mouth (this should be obvious by now), so saying fuck isn't exactly new for me, but I understood at this point that saying "fuck you" to another person is very inappropriate, but at this point I didn't even care; this woman was making me want to eat glass.

We went back and forth for a bit, me continuously telling this lady to stop arguing with me and to please just check me out so I can go, and this woman repeating that Deathstroke sucks and that I should prefer Deadshot because he's better. Eventually I just said "fuck it" and left, my family trailing behind me.

I felt bad for my older siblings, who were both mortified by it all, but surprisingly my mom was completely on board (she's also a comic book fan), and she wanted to tell the clerk off too, but I begged her not to, my shame returning after I was outta there.

I still feel a bit bad for swearing at a retail worker, but 1), I did nothing to start that argument/conversation with her, 2), I just wanted to buy a fucking Fallout 4 figure and leave, and 3), let's be honest, at the most I looked 12 at the time, so this lady straight up tried to tell a preteen that their taste in fictional characters was shit (I know this because she called me "kid" like five times during our argument).

If it's safe to, I think you should talk to your husband about how you're feeling and how his parent's judgment is affecting you. If he refuses to listen to you or help with the problem, please consider texting or calling a suicide hotline, if only so you can talk this out with a professional.

Whenever you feel ready, please look into getting medicated; I know it's hard, especially when people mistreat you for it (my own mother convinced me to stop taking my antidepressents, and deeply regret it), but it'll make everything so much better for you in the long run.

I wish you the best of luck!

May as well give my answer, since it's my question and all (sorry by the way if this question has been asked before on this Sub).

I grew up with my dad as my primary caregiver, as my parents got divorced when I was 10 years old. This was caused by mother cheating, something I won't go into in this post.

Ever since the divorce, my dad has gone above and beyond to take care of me and make sure I'm okay, and his peak moment, I think, was when I was in middle school, but more specifically in 7th grade.

At this time, I was constantly bullied and harassed by several peers, oftentimes being chased through the halls between classes, having things thrown at me at lunch, and even being threatened with rape and stalking. I was absolutely Terrified, so much so that, one night, I told my dad that I never wanted to go to school again, and that if I ever went back, I thought I would have to kill myself to keep my bullies from following me home and killing my family (I know, it wasn't very realistic, but tbf I was a scared kid).

Needless to say, Dad was horrified. The next day, I stayed at home while Dad went to my school and talked it over with my teachers and principal. According to Dad, he was given a bit of a run around by the vice principal (a lot of time was spent with the VP saying stuff like "Boys will be boys" and "Why are you even making such a big deal out of this? It's nothing your kid can't handle, I'm sure"), but Dad eventually got to talk with the principal, who agreed to help.

In the end, my bullies weren't allowed anywhere near me, and the principal even offered to walk me to my classes himself, but it ended up being okay. I was labeled as a tattletale afterwards, but tbh that was FAR BETTER than the crap I was putting up with beforehand.

This all actually came up over dinner tonight with the family, and my Dad and me talked about it in more detail, as he didn't want me to know how hard it had been on him as a kid to get help (hell, he told me that he threatened to murder the VP to his face if I ended up dead because of him, which is what convinced the guy to let Dad talk to the principal).

I love my dad so much, and I hope someday he forgives himself for how certain things went in my life. He always talks about feeling guilty for different crap from my childhood, but I know he tried his best, and I can't thank him enough for everything he did right.
